subject: Orpheus-mini onboarding - temporary version lock request & thumbprint check
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Gavin Lee <gavin.lee@openweights.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orpheus-mini onboarding - temporary version lock request & thumbprint check

Team / Gavin,

We have an inbound request from OpenWeights to bring the Orpheus-mini-8K-v2 variant into staging for a customer pilot next week. Gavin attached our standard compatibility checklist and a short tokenizer diff that shows a small tokenization divergence vs our internal BPE.

Quick summary:
- Model: Orpheus-mini-8K-v2 (3rd-party weights from OpenWeights)
- Primary ask: temporary version lock (pin) of Orpheus-mini-8K-v2 while we run a canary and tokenization/quality validation.
- Risk notes: tokenization mismatch for a subset of Chinese+emoji inputs; quantization profile recommended by vendor is int8-fp16 hybrid which we need infra signoff on.
- Proposed guardrails: 72-hour pin on hosted catalog variant, 1% traffic canary in staging, telemetry hooks for prefix hit rates, tokenization mismatch counter, and automatic rollback if latency or regression metrics exceed thresholds.

Attachments: compatibility-checklist.xlsx (vendor-provided), tokenizer-diffs.txt

My ask to the group:
- Laura: can product approve the 72-hour temporary lock and the proposed canary cadence?
- Priya: can you validate eval coverage for the tokenization regression cases?
- Connor: can infra confirm the quantization profile is safe for our runtime and whether an emergency fallback to a smaller fp16-only variant is feasible?
- Gavin: please confirm the fingerprint/thumbprint for the v2 manifest and share any micro-version that might include the tokenizer shim.

Goal: get pinned variant in staging by EOD Monday so the pilot can use a stable identifier while we finish validation.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr PM, Model Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: compatibility-checklist.xlsx]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Gavin Lee <gavin.lee@openweights.ai>
Date: 2028-04-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orpheus-mini onboarding - temporary version lock request & thumbprint check

Karthik —

Thanks for the write-up. Two clarifying Qs before I greenlight a 72-hour lock: 
1) Tokenization mismatch: how many eval prompts exercise the Chinese+emoji path? If it's low we should expand the eval set immediately; if it's common we may want to require a shim before pinning.
2) Canary window: 1% traffic in staging is fine, but for the hosted catalog pin we'll need a plan for automatic rollback and a communication note for CS if we observe any customer-facing regressions.

Priya — can you prioritize adding the tokenizer diversity cases to the regression suite and share the failing sample IDs? Connor — if quantization requires infra changes (kernel selection or different PG setup) call that out and estimate time.

If we can get the tokenizer samples and a confirm from infra that a fallback variant is available within 24 hours, I can approve the temporary pin for 72 hours and the staged canary. Otherwise we should delay the pin until we have the shim.

-Laura
Product Manager, Model Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Gavin Lee <gavin.lee@openweights.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orpheus-mini onboarding - temporary version lock request & thumbprint check

Hi team —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick notes from OpenWeights: 
- Thumbprint: sha256:5f2c3b7a9d4e8d3f6a1c2b4e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7 (manifest v2.1.0).
- Tokenizer shim: we have a patch (v2.1.1) that normalizes emoji sequences and a few CJK edge cases; it increases token counts by ~0.4% on average. We can publish a micro release but the customer pilot specifically asked for the v2.0.x interface, which is why they're requesting the pin.
- Quantization: the hybrid int8-fp16 profile has been validated on our infra; we can provide the quantization config and a short runtime test script. We recommend the fallback to fp16-only for latency-critical endpoints.

I've attached tokenizer-diffs.txt with the representative mismatches and a small test harness you can run against your tokenizer to reproduce the divergence. We're happy to cut a micro release if you prefer the shim; otherwise we understand the pilot constraints.

Gavin
Partner Engineering, OpenWeights
[gavin.lee@openweights.ai]

[Attachment: tokenizer-diffs.txt]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Gavin Lee <gavin.lee@openweights.ai>
Date: 2028-04-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orpheus-mini onboarding - temporary version lock request & thumbprint check

Appreciate the quick responses. Decision and next steps: 

1) Approve temporary 72-hour catalog variant lock for Orpheus-mini-8K-v2 (manifest sha256:5f2c3b7a9d...). Lock window: 2028-04-16T09:00:00-07:00 through 2028-04-19T09:00:00-07:00. This is explicitly for staging/catalog identifier stability only; not a permanent production pin.

2) Canaries: start with 1% traffic in staging for 24 hours, expand to 5% if no regressions. Telemetry hooks required: tokenization-mismatch counter, prefix-cache hit rate, p99 latency, and eval regression score vs baseline.

3) Priya: please add the tokenizer-diff samples to the eval run ASAP and share the failing sample IDs by EOD today.

4) Connor: if infra cannot support the hybrid profile without an emergency fallback, please schedule the fp16-only fallback variant in the same window and confirm fallback automation. If you need more time, escalate and we will retract the lock.

5) Gavin: if you can publish the micro shim (v2.1.1) before the end of the lock window we can consider replacing the pinned variant mid-window and extend the pin if it resolves the mismatch. Otherwise the pilot will proceed against v2.0.x as requested.

I'll open the INF ticket and add the telemetry dashboards (link below). Please reply inline with any objections.

Thanks,
Karthik
Sr PM, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
